object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A consignment or batch of products being tracked through the logistics network.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A tradeable item tracked by stock keeping unit.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: SKU
object_types.definition: Stock Keeping Unit - the unique identifier for a product.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The count of units for a product in a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity. For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Warehouse
object_types.definition: A physical storage location where shipments may be stored.

source_references.excerpt: Warehouses have a warehouse code.

object_types.name: WarehouseCode
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a warehouse.

source_references.excerpt: Warehouses have a warehouse code.

ambiguities.description: Product availability in shipment: Can a product appear in multiple shipments, and can the same warehouse hold multiple shipments? The model assumes yes to both, but the transcript does not explicitly confirm whether a product is ever reused across shipments or whether the Shipment-Warehouse relationship is many-to-many.

The transcript uses present tense ('sits') which suggests current state only, but no explicit confirmation that historical tracking is not required.
